content.text: {"statements": {"L5.1": {"established": "yes", "quote": "For $f(x)=x+c$ ($c\\ge 0$) the original inequalities become \\[ \\sqrt{\\frac{x^2 + (y+c)^2}{2}} \\ge \\frac{x+y+c}{2} \\ge \\sqrt{x(y+c)} ,\\] which are exactly the Quadratic‑Mean–Arithmetic‑Mean inequality and the Arithmetic‑Mean–Geometric‑Mean inequality applied to the two positive numbers $x$ and $y+c$.  Both inequalities are true for all $x,y>0$.", "note": "Both inequalities verified for all x,y and all c>=0 via QM-AM-GM."}, "L5.2": {"established": "yes", "quote": "Put $x = f(y)$ ... the chain collapses to equality: \\[\\bigl(f(f(y)) + y\\bigr)^2 = 4f(y)^2 .\\] Taking square roots (all terms are positive) yields \\[f(f(y)) + y = 2f(y)\\]", "note": "Correct substitution x=f(y); AP form (4) g(x+g(x))=g(x) also derived."}, "L5.3": {"established": "no", "quote": null, "note": "Only g(x) > -x noted; nonnegativity of g never proved, yet the dichotomy V ⊆ {0,c} tacitly assumes it."}, "L5.4": {"established": "yes", "quote": "Take $n = q t$, $m = p t$ ... Then $n c_1 - m c_2 = 0$, so the right‑hand side of (9) is the constant $(u-v-c_2)^2$, while the left‑hand side grows linearly with $t$ ... For large $t$ the inequality is violated", "note": "Both rational and irrational ratio cases handled via inequality (7) over orbits; correct."}, "L5.5": {"established": "partial", "quote": "From (11) and $x,y>0$ we obtain $(x-y)^2 > c^2$, hence \\[|x-y| > c \\qquad \\forall\\,x\\in S_0,\\;y\\in S_c . \\tag{12}\\]", "note": "Mixed-case separation, Lemma 1 and covering argument complete; but dichotomy f(x)∈{x,x+c} unproved since negative g values are never excluded."}}, "S_ref": 1, "notes": "Sufficiency (L5.1) fully verified. Necessity: equality of two positive differences is rigorous, and the fixed-point/covering exclusion is well executed, but the step from 'at most one positive value' to 'V ⊆ {0,c}' silently assumes g >= 0, which is never proved, leaving the negative-difference case uncovered."}
